patient.chief_complaint: Brief shaking at worksite, now confused and unresponsive 45 minutes later, coworker reports he fell and hit his head
patient.history_present_illness: A 48-year-old Black male construction foreman was brought to the emergency department by EMS after a witnessed fall at a construction worksite. His coworkers reported he had a brief tonic-clonic seizure lasting about 90 seconds while walking, fell to the ground, and struck the right side of his head on concrete. He was wearing no helmet (office area of the site). After the seizure stopped, he did not regain normal consciousness. EMS found him confused, agitated, GCS 10, with a visible right temporal laceration and scalp hematoma. He arrived 35 minutes after the fall. He has no prior history of seizures. Coworkers report he was acting normally at work today. No alcohol or drug use at the worksite per coworkers. He has a history of HIV infection, diagnosed 4 years ago, on antiretroviral therapy. His most recent CD4 count was 382 cells/mm3 (6 weeks ago), and his viral load was undetectable (<20 copies/mL). He takes bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (Biktarvy) daily. He also takes atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia. He has no known history of CNS opportunistic infections. His wife reports he was entirely well this morning with no complaints. No prior head trauma. Social history: former moderate drinker (quit 1 year ago), non-smoker, no illicit drugs.

results.title: Management of toxoplasmic encephalitis in HIV-infected adults
results.key_finding: Standard treatment for cerebral toxoplasmosis is pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin for 6 weeks (acute phase) followed by maintenance therapy. For patients with sulfonamide allergy, pyrimethamine + clindamycin + leucovorin is an established alternative first-line regimen. Imaging response at 2 weeks is used to confirm diagnosis; tissue biopsy is considered if no radiological improvement. Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) is a recognized risk with antiretroviral therapy optimization in active opportunistic infection.

output.summary: Cerebral toxoplasmosis is the most common space-occupying lesion in HIV-infected patients with CD4 below 200 cells/mm3, but can occur at higher CD4 counts. Empirical treatment is initiated based on clinical and radiological features; an imaging response at 2 weeks is considered confirmatory. Pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin is first-line; clindamycin-based regimens are used for sulfonamide-intolerant patients. Antiseizure medications without CYP3A4 induction are preferred in patients on certain antiretroviral regimens; levetiracetam has no significant pharmacokinetic interaction with integrase-based cART. Enzyme-inducing AEDs (phenytoin, carbamazepine) reduce exposure of certain antiretroviral drugs and are generally avoided in this context.

critical_actions: CT head immediately to exclude epidural/subdural hematoma and identify ring-enhancing lesion
Levetiracetam for AED — do NOT use phenytoin or carbamazepine (CYP induction reduces cART levels)
Serum Toxoplasma IgG and CSF Toxoplasma PCR for diagnosis
Pyrimethamine + clindamycin + leucovorin (sulfonamide allergy — cannot use sulfadiazine)
Leucovorin mandatory with pyrimethamine — prevents megaloblastic anemia
Continue cART — do NOT stop antiretroviral therapy
contraindicated_actions: Phenytoin or carbamazepine for seizure prophylaxis in HIV patient on cART — CYP3A4 induction reduces bictegravir and other antiretroviral levels dramatically
Sulfadiazine — sulfonamide allergy; use clindamycin as alternative
Stopping cART — continuation essential for immune reconstitution and toxoplasmosis control
Delaying toxoplasmosis treatment to await biopsy — empiric treatment for 2 weeks is standard; biopsy only if no response
key_reasoning_points: New seizure in HIV patient = CNS structural lesion until proven otherwise — ring-enhancing lesion is toxoplasmosis at CD4 382
Enzyme-inducing AEDs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproate to a lesser extent) reduce antiretroviral levels — levetiracetam is the safe AED in HIV
Sulfonamide allergy precludes sulfadiazine — clindamycin is the established alternative for CNS toxoplasmosis
Leucovorin is mandatory with pyrimethamine to prevent bone marrow toxicity — not optional
The contrecoup contusion explains the left NCSE on EEG — the right-sided head impact caused left temporal cortical seizure focus, not the basal ganglia toxoplasmosis lesion directly
Ring-enhancing lesion identified incidentally — it likely caused the first seizure that led to the fall; this is the primary diagnosis

red_herrings.data_point: CD4 382 cells/mm3 (above classic opportunistic infection threshold of 100-200 cells/mm3)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests toxoplasmosis is unlikely at CD4 382 (above the classic threshold of <200), prompting attribution of ring-enhancing lesion to other etiology (PCNSL, abscess) and delaying empiric toxoplasmosis treatment
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Toxoplasmosis can occur at CD4 counts up to 500 cells/mm3 in patients with high pre-existing antibody titers; Toxoplasma IgG titer 1:512 confirms prior exposure; CSF PCR positive (850 copies/mL) is definitive; empiric treatment is indicated regardless of CD4 threshold when clinical picture is consistent

red_herrings.data_point: Right-sided head impact with visible right temporal scalp laceration and hematoma — prominent traumatic mechanism
red_herrings.intended_effect: Focuses attention on traumatic etiology (post-traumatic seizure from right temporal contusion) and misses the left basal ganglia ring-enhancing lesion as the primary pathology; may prompt CT without contrast (missing ring enhancement) or attribution of all findings to trauma
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The right temporal impact caused contrecoup left temporal contusion; however, the left basal ganglia ring-enhancing lesion is non-traumatic and is best explained by HIV-associated toxoplasmosis reactivation; this lesion likely caused the initial seizure that precipitated the fall — the HIV diagnosis must redirect the diagnostic workup
